scenario.name: Combined package funded by a property-tax increase

fiscal_year_rule: FY t runs July (t-1) to June t; spending in FY t first affects calendar year t.

metrics.label: Workplace primary jobs
metrics.note: Baseline: last observed LODES JT01 year (2023) carried forward, spread from observed 2009-2023 annual changes; no ML. Change: assumption-based response modules.
metrics.target: Illustrative target: +1.0%/yr from the 2026 nowcast median

metrics.label: Resident primary-job employment
metrics.note: Residents of the 2020 town place holding a primary job anywhere in NC (LODES RAC). Not the ACS employment rate.
metrics.target: Illustrative target: +0.5%/yr from the 2026 nowcast median

metrics.label: Residents working outside town
metrics.note: NC-only share (out-of-state destinations need other states' files); held at the 2023 observed share in the baseline.

metrics.label: Operating establishments (change)
metrics.note: No townwide establishment registry, so the stock level is unavailable; only the policy-induced change is shown.

metrics.label: Relocations into town (change)
metrics.note: Relocations are not new businesses; they may move activity from elsewhere in the region.

metrics.label: Completed new homes (additional)
metrics.note: Only completions caused by the subsidy (after additionality). Baseline construction is unavailable: no completion history.

metrics.label: Housing removals
metrics.note: No demolition or conversion records were acquired.

metrics.label: Units newly restricted by preservation
metrics.note: Preservation restricts existing homes; it adds no physical units.

metrics.label: Income-restricted stock
metrics.note: Starts from 1,138 units in the FY2025 inventory (S16); most units have no recorded end date, so unknown expiries are not modelled.
metrics.target: Illustrative target: 10.0% of the housing stock anchor

metrics.label: Median gross rent
metrics.note: Level is the ACS 2019-2023 5-year anchor ($1,483), not an annual forecast. Change: transported supply elasticity.

metrics.label: Renters paying 30%+ of income
metrics.note: Needs ACS B25070 (CENSUS_API_KEY not set). No annual burden model.
metrics.target: Illustrative target: at most 40.0% of renters cost-burdened (metric unavailable)

metrics.label: Town-taxable assessed base
metrics.note: FY2026 anchor from an unaudited parcel snapshot ($12.88B); growth is an assumed range; new homes add assessed value.

metrics.label: Property-tax receipts
metrics.note: Levy = base x rate (cents) / 10,000 x collection rate. Town levy only.

metrics.label: Sales-tax distribution
metrics.note: ILLUSTRATIVE placeholder: NCDOR distribution history (S45) not acquired. Policies do not change it here.

metrics.label: Comparable operating expenditure
metrics.note: ILLUSTRATIVE baseline (balanced FY2026 reference grown by assumed cost inflation) plus exact policy payments.

metrics.label: Operating balance
metrics.target: Illustrative target: operating balance of at least $0

metrics.label: Fund balance, % of expenditure
metrics.target: Illustrative target: fund balance of at least 8.0% of expenditure (8% is the commonly cited NC Local Government Commission minimum; verify)

metrics.label: Funding gap (unfunded requests)
metrics.note: Requested spending that no legally available source could cover (no borrowing).

history.source: LODES8 JT01 (S24), 2020 Chapel Hill place blocks

policies.title: Small-Business Support Grant
policies.mechanism: Eligible existing establishments apply; awards are capped by budget and applications. A grant lowers a recipient's closure hazard by a dose-dependent amount that can be zero. Only avoided closures count, net of displacement of competitors; most funded businesses would have stayed open anyway.
policies.delays: Effects start in the award year; saved establishments then face ordinary closure risk.
policies.constraints: Recipients are capped by the assumed eligible stock and take-up; unspent budget is reported.
policies.missing_evidence: Applicant, award, rejection and survival records (Town Economic Development, Orange County).

policies.title: New-Business Startup Grant
policies.mechanism: Applications -> eligible awards -> disbursement -> incremental openings after additionality. Openings are split into new establishments and relocations; survival and competitor crowd-out follow.
policies.delays: Openings occur one year after the award; first-year survival is below later survival.
policies.constraints: Awards are capped by eligible applications and budget.
policies.missing_evidence: Applicant and award histories with actual opening and survival dates.

policies.title: Hiring Subsidy
policies.mechanism: Subsidised qualifying hires minus deadweight (hires that would happen anyway) and substitution give additional workplace jobs; resident employment rises only by the share filled by town residents.
policies.delays: Jobs persist while subsidised; after support ends a retention share survives, then separations continue.
policies.constraints: Qualifying hires are capped by the eligible hiring pool, budget and labour availability.
policies.missing_evidence: Employer contracts, reimbursed wages, headcount/retention outcomes and comparison cohorts.

policies.title: Housing Construction Subsidy
policies.mechanism: Budget funds units up to an assumed feasible capacity. Funded projects move through the pipeline and complete after a delay drawn from the town's observed approval-to-completion lags (S13), at least one year; some fail. Only the additional share adds housing supply; restrictions apply to funded units and expire after the chosen term. Preservation restricts existing homes and adds no units.
policies.delays: No same-year homes: completions follow funding by one to five years.
policies.constraints: Zoning, sewer capacity, flood, wetland and soil constraints were not acquired; an assumed annual capacity cap stands in and is labelled. Half the award is paid at funding, half at completion; the unpaid half is encumbered.
policies.missing_evidence: Complete permit/certificate-of-occupancy histories, financing stacks and OWASA capacity decisions.

policies.title: Property Tax Adjustment
policies.mechanism: Town levy = town-taxable base x rate in cents per $100 / 10,000, times a collection rate. Only the town component changes; county, school and district rates are separate. Lower taxes are not assumed to cause growth.
policies.delays: Applies from the effective fiscal year for the chosen duration.
policies.constraints: The base is an unaudited current parcel snapshot grown by an assumed rate.
policies.missing_evidence: Annual assessment rolls, exemptions and collection history.

benchmark.note: Targets are goals, not causal counterfactuals; gaps to target are not policy effects.

assumptions.note: Townwide small establishments eligible for support. No establishment registry was acquired (dossier S33-S36).
Share of eligible establishments that apply in a funded year.
Annual establishment exit rate, in the range of national Business Dynamics Statistics rates (S34, not acquired locally).
Largest relative cut in a recipient's closure hazard; scaled by grant size with diminishing returns. Can be zero.
Grant size giving half of the maximum hazard reduction.
Share of avoided closures offset by competitors' closures.
Primary jobs per small local establishment.
Startup applications per funded year. County Business Formation Statistics (S35) were not acquired.
Share of applications meeting eligibility.
Share of awardees that would not otherwise open in town.
Share of incremental openings that are relocations, not new establishments.
Survival through the first year of operation (BDS-like range).
Annual exit hazard after the first year.
Competitor closures per incremental opening.
Primary jobs per new establishment.
Gross hires per workplace job. QWI hire rates (S31) were not acquired.
Share of baseline hires at eligible employers/positions.
Subsidised hires that would have happened anyway.
Additional hires offset by fewer unsubsidised hires.
Additional jobs still filled one year after support ends.
Annual separation of retained additional jobs.
Cap on additional hires per year from labour availability.
Feasible subsidisable units per year. Zoning, sewer capacity (OWASA), flood and soil layers were not acquired.
Share of funded new units that would not be built without the subsidy (financing-gap additionality).
Funded projects cancelled before completion.
Assessed value added per completed new unit.
Rent change per % change in housing stock: Li (2022) -0.1; Mense (2025) -0.19 (as cited in data/assumptions.json). Transported from other markets; not a Chapel Hill estimate.
Current-year collection rate. Audited collection history (S42) was blocked.
Behavioural response of the taxable base to the town rate. Fixed at 0: not identified; lower taxes are not assumed to cause growth.
Nominal growth of the town-taxable base between revaluations. No assessment history was acquired.
Nominal growth of comparable operating expenditure.
Residents working in town / town workplace primary jobs, LODES 2023 (S24).

label: Sensitivity simulation: policy effects are assumption-based, not validated local causal predictions.

attribution.method: removal comparison (final year, median of paired differences)
attribution.note: Contributions can sum to more or less than the total when cards share budgets, reserves or capacity.

explanation.text:
By 2031, with Small-Business Support Grant, New-Business Startup Grant, Hiring Subsidy, Housing Construction Subsidy, Property Tax Adjustment:
- workplace jobs: median change 55 jobs (80% interval 41 to 71; basis: assumption).
- resident jobs: median change 6 jobs (80% interval 5 to 8; basis: assumption).
- housing net stock change: median change 59 units (80% interval 29 to 88; basis: assumption).
- restricted stock: median change 50 units (80% interval 25 to 75; basis: assumption).
- receipts property tax: median change 3,662,946 $ (80% interval 3,525,330 to 3,800,034; basis: arithmetic).
- policy disbursements: median change 2,000,000 $ (80% interval 1,000,000 to 3,000,000; basis: arithmetic).
- operating balance: median change 1,697,576 $ (80% interval 725,702 to 2,716,717; basis: arithmetic).
Warning: Unmet demand: small-business grant applicants were not funded in some years.
Sensitivity simulation: policy effects are assumption-based, not validated local causal predictions.
